_comment: Opt-in authored tow lanes + cart parking spot for the COUPLED restock drives. Merge the 'navigation.tow_lanes'/'navigation.directional_zone' keys into the mission runtime-config's navigation block, and the 'mission_poses.cart_parking' pose into mission_poses (the integration/bt-driver lane wires the return nav goal + uncouple step on that key). Absent => coupled drives free-plan exactly as before (byte-identical) and the braking gate uses the direction-aware zone by default. Poses are map-frame [x, y, yaw] in metres/radians; yaw PI = facing -x (west), 0 = facing +x (east), -PI/2 = facing -y (south), +PI/2 = facing +y (north). Waypoints are the authored centreline the expanded trajectory must pass through (asserted at build time). goal_articulation is the lane's achievable terminal cart articulation and governs arrival when the lane is active.
_dock_align_note: sim-dock-align-v1: the couple dock is RE-HEADED to face SOUTH on the portal axis so the coupled train never does a REORIENTATION in the warehouse backroom. BEFORE (east-facing dock [-4.46, 15.25, 0]): the train coupled facing EAST and swung a ~46 deg coupled-articulation reorientation LOOP at the throat to turn south into the portal (outbound backroom articulation max 46.1 deg, loop_ratio 2.28 -- a 21.3 m path for an 8.5 m direct); the OLD return likewise turned ~42.5 deg coupled in the backroom to reach the far west parking spot [-9, 16] -- these backroom reorientations are the rotation the captain saw. AFTER: the outbound lane STARTS at the south-facing portal-axis dock [-3.875, 14.5, -PI/2] with the cart already aligned behind it (start_cart_yaw -PI/2), so the train couples aligned and drives STRAIGHT south -- backroom articulation 0.0 deg, loop_ratio 1.22 -- crossing the wall opening (y=11.125) dead-centre at robot articulation 0.0 deg, 0.586 m clearance per side. The return mirrors it: tows the cart north and parks it on the portal axis at cart_parking [-3.875, 16.3, +PI/2] (robot north of the cart in the receiving/turning zone ~4 m back from the doorway; it uncouples and exits sideways UNCOUPLED -- a turn with no cart attached), backroom articulation 3.2 deg, loop_ratio 1.09, cart crosses the opening aligned (~1 deg). MEASURED (CPU, twin.mobile train envelope, 798-obstacle static map, data/sim-dock-align-v1/): the BACKROOM + DOCK + robot wall-crossing is <=3.6 deg both ways (the captain's win). The whole-lane MAX stays ~46 deg at the sales-floor SHELF-SERVICE turn, INHERENT to the externally-fixed endcap service pose [-3.05, 6.0, PI] (0.825 m EAST of the portal axis, facing west, so delivering the coupled cart there needs a sharp in-aisle turn regardless of the dock; goal_articulation < 0.78 does not expand). On the OUTBOUND that turn begins immediately south of the wall, so the cart's TAIL finishes its pass through the opening angled up to ~40 deg (unchanged from BEFORE's 40.7 deg; a property of the shelf goal, not the dock) -- the swept envelope stays wall-clear (no wedge, ~0.8 m each side). Follow-up to pull the outbound cart's doorway transit straight too: relocate shelf_approach to a sales-floor staging pose on the portal axis + a separate uncoupled service leg, OR move the endcap service pose (store planogram) -- integration-owned.
_couple_handoff_note: STATION geometry the integration lane wires to match the new lane start (mission runtime-config mission_poses, external): keep the couple APPROACH a SEPARATE navigation step ending in a straight reverse (captain-approved shape). Recommended south-facing couple poses on the portal axis -- robot faces south, cart staged NORTH of it facing south (hitch pointing south toward the robot rear), robot reverses NORTH to seat: couple_standoff [-3.875, 14.1, -PI/2] (on the cart axis, ~0.4 m south of the dock, TIGHT xy arrival; the fine-dock insert reverses north onto the drawbar), couple_approach [-3.875, 13.0, -PI/2] (on-axis, clear south of the staged cart). Post-couple the robot sits at the lane start [-3.875, 14.5, -PI/2] with the cart centre at [-3.875, 15.77] (1.27 m aligned separation, clear of the backroom racks at y>=17.87). Stage the cart (initial_staging cart_body_pose + unit_yaws_world.cart) at that pose facing south. cart_parking_backaway: after the return parks + uncouples, the robot (north of the parked cart, boxed from the racks) turns UNCOUPLED and exits east/west along y~16.3 to home -- any uncoupled pose that clears the parked cart, e.g. [-5.2, 16.3, PI]. Tune all couple poses against the measured pinned cart with couple_cart_relative (docs/examples/couple-approach-mission-fragment.json).
_gpu_handoff_note: For a tow-through-portal GPU proof the integration lane should ALSO set the top-level scene-build key portal_floor_box=true (flat drive-floor box collider -- removes the from-rest caster ghost-contact pin, sim-robust-portal-floor-seam-v1) and keep the coupled_heading_hold / heading_hold_prethroat_m / heading_hold_launch_m keys from docs/examples/throat-momentum-launch-mission-fragment.json. Those address the from-rest dock pin, which the geometry change does not; the geometry change gives the straight passage. ACCEPTANCE (couple + outbound + return): the coupled train couples south-aligned on the portal axis and drives STRAIGHT through the backroom + dock + wall crossing (<=3.6 deg coupled articulation through the whole backroom passage, robot dead-centre in the opening, >=0.5 m clearance each side), no from-rest pin, no doorway wedge (swept envelope wall-clear even where the outbound cart tail exits the opening angled up to ~40 deg as the sales-floor shelf turn begins); the whole-lane max articulation ~46 deg occurs ONLY at the sales-floor shelf-service turn, south of the wall (inherent to the external shelf pose, unchanged before/after). nav_towing_check / towing_check are the GPU validations of the straight crossing (both already assume a portal-aligned dock + a 0.80 rad / 46 deg jackknife guard the straight backroom passage clears with margin; the shelf-turn terminal ~0.80 rad is unchanged from the pre-existing lane).
_fm437_note: tow_lane_trust_unknown (default off): on a static-validated authored lane, trust UNOBSERVED temporal-map cells in the swept envelope as free (the static map proved that corridor clear); a POSITIVE/occupied return still stops the tow.
_fm454_note: fm454 (option b): both tow lanes set route_through_waypoints=true. expand() routes the train THROUGH the authored via-poses as ordered sub-goals so the realised trajectory IS the authored corner (a straight portal crossing forced by the on-axis south/north via-poses), not a free-plan that merely passes near it. route_through_waypoints absent/false => free-plan-and-validate, byte-identical to the historical lane.
